transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-06-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Marissa Cole (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sarah Lee (Regional BankCorp - Head of Cloud Ops), Tom Nguyen (Security Engineer), Priya Patel (Compliance Manager)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on data residency and compliance needs for production inference: customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments, must meet financial services controls, GDPR and specific logging/audit restrictions. Agreed next steps: share compliance artifacts, run small benchmark, collect in-scope regs.

Topics:
- Data residency requirements (EU/US zones and customer data never leaving country)
- Logging and audit log retention (SIEM integration, PII filtering)
- Encryption and KMS (HSM requirement for keys)
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Timeline and success criteria for pilot

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marissa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Marissa Cole from Redwood, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Sarah: Hi Marissa, hi Diego. Thanks for fitting us in. We wanted to use this time to walk through our requirements around data residency and auditability.
[00:15] Diego: Absolutely. Quick question up front, are you evaluating this for a pilot in production or just POC internal tooling?
[00:21] Priya: The ask from compliance is production-facing. We will be using the models for customer support automation and some KYC triage, so higher bar.
[00:29] Tom: Security is especially concerned about logs—what's sent to Redwood, what's stored, and how long it's retained.
[00:35] Marissa: Totally understood. Maybe I can quickly run through the three deployment modes and the typical trade-offs. Hosted is quick to get started, but we know retention and export policies are important. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and better isolation, and Private gives you a VPC/private control plane or even on-prem if needed.
[00:50] Sarah: We have a strict requirement that EU customer PII must not leave EU borders. So for any EU data we need residency in EU infrastructure and legal assurances.
[00:58] Diego: Right, we can route requests to EU regions and we do offer Private deployments where the control plane is customer-managed. For financial services customers we often recommend Dedicated or Private depending on SLA and audit needs.
[01:10] Priya: One more thing—our auditors require that encryption keys are under our control, ideally HSM-backed KMS. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[01:18] Marissa: Yes, we support KMS integrations; for Private and Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM solutions. For Hosted there are options but fewer guarantees around customer-owned hardware keys.
[01:30] Tom: Can you be specific—if we pick Dedicated with reserved capacity in eu-west-1, will the model logs still flow through a Redwood control plane in the US? We need to avoid that.
[01:39] Diego: Good callout. For Dedicated we can configure regional control plane endpoints and data paths so that request bodies and logs stay within the region. There are legacy cases where some telemetry funnels to centralized metrics, but for regulated customers we set up regional logging and a push model into your SIEM.
[01:56] Sarah: Ok, and what about retention—our policy is 7 years for certain transaction logs and 1 year for others. We can't have automatic deletion outside of our retention policies.
[02:05] Marissa: We can support configurable retention policies and export hooks. The practical constraint is for Hosted we have default retention windows; Dedicated/Private give you explicit control.
[02:12] Tom: How do you handle PII in logs? We don't want full prompts or answers stored in naked form.
[02:17] Diego: We offer masking/on-the-fly redaction plugins, and you can opt for token-level trimming or prefix-only caching. There is a trade-off: redaction can impact debugging.
[02:26] Priya: Our auditors also want an append-only audit log with integrity proofs and rotation records. Is that available?
[02:33] Marissa: We provide audit logs that can be exported to your SIEM, and for Private deployments you can host the storage backend so you retain full control. Integrity proofs are usually handled by your internal storage. We can integrate with systems that provide immutable storage hooks.
[02:47] Sarah: Excellent. One of the things we're trying to nail down is whether we can use Redwood Hosted for non-PII workloads and push PII workloads to Dedicated or Private. Is that a common pattern?
[02:57] Diego: Yes, that's a common hybrid approach—route redacted or public queries to Hosted to save cost, and route sensitive traffic to Dedicated or Private with enforced routing rules.
[03:07] Tom: About encryption in transit—do you do mutual TLS to the dedicated pools? We require mTLS for internal services.
[03:12] Diego: We support mTLS for Dedicated/Private endpoints and customer-managed certificates. For Hosted API it's standard TLS, and we can do IP allowlisting and VPC peering for additional network isolation.
[03:23] Priya: GDPR-wise, we need the data processing addendum and assurance that subprocessors are listed. Can you share the DPA and subprocessor list?
[03:31] Marissa: Absolutely, we'll send the DPA and current subprocessor list. We'll also include SOC 2 and ISO summaries.
[03:37] Sarah: Are there any certifications that Redwood has specific to financial services? We often look for SOC 2 Type II and support for PCI scopes.
[03:43] Marissa: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO alignment. PCI is usually a customer-level scope—we can help with architecture to keep card data out of the model flow.
[03:52] Tom: One operational question: if we do Dedicated, how are rollouts handled? We want canary deploys and quick rollback if a model release causes regressions.
[03:59] Diego: Our console supports canary and A/B rollouts, model pinning, and automatic fallback to earlier variants. For Dedicated you get more control over rollout windows and metrics thresholds.
[04:09] Sarah: Cost—how should we think about cost when comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? We have throughput peaks during month end and cost spikes are a concern.
[04:19] Marissa: Hosted is pay-as-you-go and easiest, Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable commitments—you can add burst capacity. Private is typically higher fixed cost but gives best isolation. We also provide Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce token spend.
[04:31] Tom: For the month-end spikes—do you have autoscaling that can burst into cloud spot pools? We need predictable performance during spikes.
[04:38] Diego: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity; we can coordinate capacity planning with you. Burst into spot can work but you'd still keep a baseline reserved.
[04:47] Priya: Our auditors will want to see the logging schema and an example audit trail. Can we get sample logs and a mapping to our SIEM fields?
[04:54] Marissa: Yes, we'll provide sample logs and a mapping doc. Diego, can you lead on the sample log extract?
[05:00] Diego: Yep, I'll pull a sanitized example and show how fields map to common SIEMs.
[05:05] Sarah: Are there any gotchas when sending prompts that contain SSNs or account numbers?
[05:09] Diego: We recommend pre-processing to tokenize or redact sensitive identifiers client-side. We do not offer guaranteed automatic PII detection in all cases—so best practice is to send redacted content for Hosted and rely on Dedicated/Private for stronger controls.
[05:21] Tom: For Private/on-prem—what's the typical deployment footprint? We're thinking of a small cluster that integrates with our existing Kubernetes and our HSM.
[05:28] Marissa: For an on-prem Private deployment we provide an appliance-like manifest, and the runtime can be run in your K8s cluster. Diego will share sizing guidelines—GPU counts, memory, and I/O requirements.
[05:36] Diego: For the models you described, a modest cluster with 4 GPUs can suffice for pilot traffic; we'll give exact numbers after we run a quick workload profile.
[05:45] Priya: About auditors—do you provide attestations or support calls for audits? We sometimes need vendor attestations.
[05:50] Marissa: We support audit support and will provide the SOC 2 report under NDA; for deeper attestation we can coordinate with partners or professional services.
[05:59] Sarah: Timeline—if we want to pilot in July, what's realistic?
[06:03] Marissa: If you can share in-scope regs and a sample workload this week, we can scope a pilot and target mid-July for an initial pilot. Diego would run a short benchmark early to validate latency and logging paths.
[06:14] Tom: One more technical: does Redwood keep KV cache across requests or is cache ephemeral? We worry about long-lived caches keeping PII.
[06:21] Diego: KV cache is an in-memory runtime optimization; we never persist KV cache to long-term storage. For added safety we can disable prefix caching or set TTLs.
[06:30] Sarah: Ok, good. Can you share a list of default and optional telemetry that Redwood collects? We need to confirm what's unavoidable.
[06:37] Marissa: We'll send the telemetry list—default metrics, traces, and options to opt out of some telemetry in Dedicated/Private.
[06:43] Priya: Regarding legal—contracting is done through our procurement team and we typically require a data processing addendum and specific SLAs. Any blockers there?
[06:52] Marissa: No blockers. We'll provide standard enterprise contracts and can work with procurement. Procurement questions often drive the Dedicated/Private decision.
[06:59] Diego: Quick note on integrations—we support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and RBAC for role separation. For audit we can push user activity logs to your SIEM.
[07:12] Tom: Great. Are there any limitations on models in Private? Sometimes newer open models have special runtime needs.
[07:18] Diego: We try to support a broad catalog, but some bleeding-edge models require specific kernel support. We'll list supported models for Private deployments; if you need a model not supported out-of-the-box we can onboard it as part of a customer success engagement.
[07:30] Sarah: Ok that covers most of our compliance questions. What's the realistic next step?
[07:35] Marissa: We'll send the DPA, SOC 2, ISO docs, sample logs, and pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Diego will schedule a 30-minute benchmark/technical check-in with Tom next week.
[07:45] Tom: Sounds good. Can we get an initial bill of materials/sizing for an on-prem pilot?
[07:49] Diego: Yes, I'll include a sizing doc in the follow-up.
[07:53] Priya: We'll also send the list of in-scope regs and the auditors' contact if needed.
[07:57] Marissa: Perfect. One last question—are there any concerns on your side we haven't touched?
[08:01] Sarah: Not yet. I just want to make sure the controls are auditable and that we have clear isolation between EU and US data.
[08:08] Marissa: Understood. We'll include networking diagrams and data flow patterns in the follow-up.
[08:13] Diego: I'll put together the benchmark plan and sanitized sample logs.
[08:17] Marissa: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts by Thursday. Appreciate your time.
[08:23] Sarah: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:26] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[08:30] Priya: Bye.
